configs.description: CCR2004-1G-12S+2XS - twelve SFP+ cages, two SFP28 cages, a gigabit management jack and an RJ45 console, with two AC supplies and two fans (all part of the chassis in this model). The box holds two IEC cords, rack ears and a fastening set.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: No dimensions drawing is held; the front is read off studio photograph 1937, which looks down on it, so x is photo-measured and y is estimated.

No rear view is held (NetBox has no rear elevation for this model); the rear is read off studio photograph 1936, which looks down on it, so the y positions are estimated. The heatsink block and its fins stand out of the rear plane; their depth is not held, so the block is drawn flat inside the face.

The brochure gives 49 W maximum; the product page gives 60 W maximum and 31 W without attachments. The brochure's 49 W is carried as the maximum, the page's 60 W is kept as power-max-w-page, and the 31 W is the page's figure without attachments and is not a maximum.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's statement of the maximum consumption.

gaps.note: The brochure says a dual redundant power supply is included and "Number of AC inputs 2"; the page lists no PSU slots; no held document prints a supply part number or shows a module. The two supplies are part of the chassis with their inlets and no bay is added; the base configuration exports two power ports.
gaps.wanted: The supply's part number and a statement of what is replaceable.

gaps.note: The page says 2 fans and the rear photograph shows two round fan openings and a finned heatsink block. The block is drawn as chassis art and not counted as a fan; no document says whether it is cooled by either fan, and none states a fan redundancy form.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's fan count and cooling description.

gaps.note: The slots are drawn as measured, but the metal's band is a recess whose lower edge sweeps down from the left end and back up at the right end, and the slots the sweep shortens are cut along that curve. No decor draws a curved edge, so the shortened slots are cut square and the curve is not drawn: they are up to about 0.8 mm off.
gaps.wanted: A dimensioned front view, or a decor edge that follows a curve.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: The brochure says "dual redundant power supply" and "Number of AC inputs 2"; the page says "Number of AC inputs 2" and lists no PSU slots. No held document prints a supply part number and photograph 1936 shows two plain C14 inlets with wire clips and no module, handle or latch, so the supplies are part of the chassis with their inlets and no bay is drawn. The page says "Cooling type 2 fans" and the photograph shows two round fan openings, one after the second inlet and one at the right of the heatsink; the finned heatsink block between them is chassis art, not a third fan (as the CRS309's is).

chassis.note: 443 x 224 x 44 mm: the brochure and the product page print the same figures. The width is the full ear-to-ear width as printed (the ears ship flush). No drawing is held, so it cannot be checked whether the 224 includes what stands off the rear: the wire retaining clips of the inlets stand off the rear edge in photographs 1935 and 1937, and the depth is carried as printed, taken as the body with the retaining clips not counted (assumed, not measured).

colour.note: The face and the fan hubs are drawn #c4c4c4, the samples listed under colour-sample: photograph 1937's median is #c5c3c3 and the brochure's front figure is #c4c4c4. The rear photograph 1936 reads #c5c5c5 over x 1215 to 1420, y 972 to 1103 (26855 pixels); the brochure's rear figure reads lighter (#d1d1d1), so the rear's colour is the more lit of the two and not taken. The heatsink, all on photograph 1936, y 888 to 1100 (the block's top edge to the face's bottom edge): the base between the fins is #414142, the median of 121688 pixels over the twenty gaps (x from 8 px after one fin's centre to 8 px before the next, 1865 to 2699 across the block); the gap is a gradient from #676769 at the top to #303030 at the bottom and the median of the whole is drawn. The fin face is #a6a5a5, the median of 13356 pixels in 3 px columns at the 21 fin centres. The left rim is #d9d9d9 (6996 pixels over x 1740 to 1773) and the right rim #9a9a98 (2120 pixels over x 2751 to 2761).

colour-sample.note: Face #c4c4c4: the median of 52220 pixels of photograph 1937 over x 2492 to 2865, y 995 to 1135 (plain face, right of the lamp legends) is #c5c3c3, and of 11400 pixels of the brochure's front figure (fig. 2) over x 1130 to 1320, y 285 to 345 is #c4c4c4. The management plate #787674 is the median of 1040 pixels of photograph 1937 over x 2215 to 2295, y 1037 to 1050 (between the two jacks); the SFP28 strip #898784 is the median of 92 pixels over x 597 to 620, y 1054 to 1058. The lamps' colours belong to the component skins and are not changed here.

datasheet.note: Brochure specifications: product code CCR2004-1G-12S+2XS, AL32400 1700 MHz, 4 cores, 4 GB DDR4, 128 MB NAND, 1 gigabit Ethernet port, 12 SFP+ ports, 2 SFP28 ports (25G), RouterOS v7 license level 6, AC power supply 100 - 240 V, 2 AC inputs, 443 x 224 x 44 mm, -20 to +60 C tested, 49 W maximum; included: 2 IEC cords, rackmount bracket white, fastening set for rackmount case. The page adds 60 W maximum, 31 W without attachments and 2 fans.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (brochure: Rackmount bracket white). They ship flush with the face and are not drawn.

front-layout.note: From photograph 1937 at 3.30 px per mm in x. SFP28 stack: cage left at 15.4 mm, upper cage top at 11.5 mm and lower at 27.5 mm (a 16.0 mm row pitch), with a grey strip between the cages that carries four printed arrows. SFP+ cages: 15.2 mm wide, first centre at 43.0 mm, 19.8 mm pitch, top at 27.4 mm. The console and management jacks sit in one 17.6 x 27.0 mm plate at 277.7 mm; RESET at 299.7 mm. The plates are drawn at the photograph's median over each (see colour).

gate-1.note: No drawing is held. Photograph 1937's body is 1462 px across at the displayed 2000 px width for the printed 443 (3.30 px per mm); x is taken at that scale from the body's left edge, measured on crops at 9.8 px per mm. The photograph looks down on the chassis, so the face is foreshortened by about 8 percent (the face is 133 px for 44 mm, 3.02 px per mm): y is measured up from the face's bottom edge and is estimated. The SFP+ pitch reads 19.81 mm across eleven steps (43.0 to 260.9 mm), on a quantity the scale never saw.

lamps.note: Each SFP+ cage has an ACT lamp 5.2 mm left of its centre and a 10G lamp 4.4 mm right of it, both 4.6 x 2.6 mm as drawn on the metal, with ACT and 10G printed above. The SFP28 stack has four arrows (down, up, down, up) in its strip, printed with 1 and 2 beneath. The four chassis lamps (USER, FAULT, PWR 2, PWR 1) are at 307.3 mm. No held document says what a lamp shows.

legends.note: The front legends are set at 2.3 mm. Each cap height was read on photograph 1937: USER, SFP+ 1, CONSOLE and MGMT/BOOT are 10 to 12 px tall at 5.59 px per mm up the face (1.8 to 2.1 mm of cap), and the face's wider letter shapes fix the size by width: USER is 38 px and MGMT/BOOT 92 px across at 6.106 px per mm, 6.2 and 15.1 mm, which DejaVu draws at 2.3 mm. The SFP28 labels (1, 2 and 25G SFP28) are set at 1.9 mm, their width in the photograph. The rear's rating line on photograph 1936 is 207 px, 33.4 mm, across at 6.19 px per mm, which 2.2 mm draws, so the rear legends are 2.2 mm. The model text keeps its size.

port-numbering.note: SFP+ 1 to SFP+ 12 are printed under the cages, left to right. The SFP28 stack prints 1 with a down arrow and 2 with an up arrow under it, as the CRS518 prints its stacks, so the lower cage is 1 and the upper 2. MGMT/BOOT is printed under the lower of the two stacked jacks and CONSOLE, with an arrow, beside the upper, so the management jack (the brochure's one gigabit port) is the lower one and the console the upper.

rear-layout.note: estimated - no rear elevation is held; the positions are read off photograph 1936 (crop at 4.33 px per mm). It looks down on the rear, so x is good to about 1.5 mm and y, from the face's bottom edge, to about 2.5 mm. Inlets at 31.0 and 111.6 mm with POWER 1 or 2 and the rating line under each; fan openings 37 mm across at 170.2 and 385.5 mm. The heatsink block, re-read on photograph 1936 at 6.124 px per mm (the body's 2713 px at the fins, left edge 515 px): a thick rim 200.0 to 205.0 mm, 21 fins every 7.31 mm (44.75 px), the first centred at 211.95 mm, each 1.4 mm wide (the run of the fin's bright face is 8 to 10 px, 1.3 to 1.6 mm), and a thin rim at 365.0 to 366.9 mm, so the block is 166.9 mm wide from 200.0 mm. Drawn as a grey base with one silver rectangle per fin, full height. Photograph 1936 and the brochure's rear figure (fig. 3) show the fins reaching past the box's lower edge: the camera looks down and the block stands out of the rear plane, so it is the block's depth, not a lower edge; the depth is not held and the block is drawn flat inside the rear face. The guards are honeycombs (hexagonal holes round a hub), read on photograph 1936 at 18.37 px per mm in a 3x crop: hexagons 5.3 mm across corners (the camera looks down, so its flats read 4.1 mm where a regular hexagon of that width is 4.6), 5.06 mm between columns, so a lattice of 5.88 mm centre to centre down a column, with a hexagon at the hub's centre and the one whole ring of hexagons round it cut by the opening's circle. Drawn as `motif`, one tile of two columns (10.184 x 5.88 mm) holding hexagons 5.36 mm across corners, with the tile's origin at the fan's centre. The plain `vent` pattern ties the hexagon to its pitch: scaled to this 5.88 mm pitch its web is 0.8 mm where the photograph's is about 1.3, so it draws the metal too fat. The inlets' wire retaining clips and the screws are not drawn (no registry part).

side-layout.note: Photograph 1935 shows the left wall plain: a screw and a few holes, no vent or grille. No held photograph shows the right wall.

vent-band.note: estimated - measured on photograph 1937 at 6.106 px per mm across (the body's 2705 px at the band for the printed 443 mm; the body's left edge at 507.5 px) and 5.59 px per mm up the face (the face is 246 px for 44 mm because the camera looks down). The band is 60 parallel slots leaning right, one every 4.736 mm (28.92 px, 59 steps from 589 px to 2295 px), the first slot's top-left corner at 13.35 mm. A full slot is 2.4 mm wide across and 9.3 mm tall, its foot 2.70 mm left of its top, with corners cut 0.3 mm for the rounded ends. The slots' tops are at 4.9 mm; the lower edge of the band sweeps down from the left end and back up at the right end. Drawn as: the 41 full slots 11 to 51 as one `motif` field with a 4.736 x 9.3 mm tile holding one slot (it is 2.4 + 2.70 = 5.1 mm across, so its corner wraps into the next tile and is cut in two); five dashes at each end (slots 1 to 5 and 56 to 60, 2.5 mm tall) as one `motif` field each with a 4.736 x 2.5 mm tile; and the slots the sweep shortens, 6 to 10 and 52 to 55, each as its own one-tile `motif` rect at the height measured at its foot (2.9, 4.1, 5.9, 7.7 and 8.8 mm on the left; 8.9, 7.7, 5.4 and 3.2 mm on the right). No source draws the sweep's outline, and the foot of each shortened slot is cut square: the metal cuts it along the curve, up to about 0.8 mm off. The `vent` hexagons do not draw any of it. Every tile is 0.2 mm taller than the slot it holds, with the cells 0.1 mm inside its top and bottom edges and the tile begun 0.1 mm above the field: a cell on a tile edge left a faint 1 px seam between the slots along it. The one slot of the main field is 4.93 mm across, wider than the 4.736 mm pitch, so it is still cut where it crosses the tile's side edge.
